summary: Frontend-only parity verification of the iter342 motion + Guided Journeys reorder + Timeline redesign + Family Wall restyle batch on both web and mobile. All nine review items PASSED on both surfaces. Login sign-in overlay + self-drawing loader render on submit (both wrong and correct password on web; overlay visible with 'Signing you in...' spinner on mobile). Layout.wayly-page-in wrapper confirmed present on the web dashboard. Guided Journeys sidebar order (web) and drawer order (mobile) both match the spec exactly, including the 'SAH Classification Prep' rename. Timeline redesign works end-to-end on both platforms: cards collapsed by default (0 bodies), search filter + 6 filter chips present, tapping a card reveals the timeline-event-body. Family Wall renders with the calm cream/surface background + single subtle teal left accent (verified via inline style borderLeft on web and borderLeftColor: colors.primary on mobile). Calendar Required/Optional labels still present on web (verified in Add-entry modal screenshot).

ui_bugs.issue: The svg root inside the login sign-in overlay does not expose testID 'login-loader' as a queryable data-testid attribute in the Expo web preview (query returned null while the spinner is clearly rendered on screen). Non-blocking — overlay itself (login-signing-overlay) is present and the loader is visible. Consider forwarding testID onto the outer wrapper View (which is a real DOM node) so parity with web is testable programmatically. Reference: /app/mobile/src/components/WaylyLoader.tsx

action_items: (Optional / low priority) Forward mobile WaylyLoader testID onto a native View wrapper so automation can assert the loader element separately from the overlay in the Expo web preview.
critical_code_review_comments: Family Wall (web) uses an inline style borderLeft:'4px solid rgba(14,77,82,0.5)'. It works, but for theming consistency consider extracting to a token/class (e.g. .wall-post-accent) so dark mode / future palette shifts don't need per-file edits.

Web Guided Journeys group renders on load without needing the group to be expanded explicitly for tests, but bandwidth-heavy 'wait_for_load_state networkidle' consistently times out on this app — non-blocking, only affects automation. Consider a Cypress-style route-idle marker (data-testid page-ready) for future testability.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter342 batch (motion + nav reorder + timeline redesign + wall restyle + calendar label parity) verified on both web and mobile. No blockers. Next testing pass need only revisit if a NEW change lands. Web login: cathy@example.com / testpass123. Mobile drawer opens via bottom 'More' tab (not swipe) in the Expo web preview.
